A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Dyn-VQA/OmniSearch study, including Appendices A–E. Text, tables and figures support reliable comparison; the rasterized example in v4 Figure 3 remains visually readable.

before.justification: v3 reports original model evaluations, human performance measurements, ablations and error analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains the original benchmark results in Table 4 and the experimental analyses throughout the appendices.

M1.justification: The planning agent, multimodal retriever, sub-question solver and GPT-4V/Qwen-VL-Chat implementations remain unchanged. Removing the prompt templates changes documentation without establishing a changed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 1,452-question, bilingual, nine-domain Dyn-VQA dataset and retain evaluation on VQAv2, A-OKVQA and InfoSeek. Training data sources and represented question categories also remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 4 and the extended benchmark table retain the same backbone models, heuristic retrieval variants, Bing Chat, Perplexity AI, Gemini, and human/golden-query comparisons. The added agentic-RAG discussion introduces no evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: The F1-Recall evaluation, training settings, retrieved-content controls, solver configurations and GPT/human evaluation procedures are unchanged. No new experiment or explicit revision to an existing setting is reported.

E4.justification: Solver swaps, retrieved-content ablations, top-k sensitivity tests, metric comparisons, domain and prediction-overlap analyses, computational-cost analyses and failure cases are retained. The analysis of 100 errors in Appendix E.3 is also unchanged.

E5.justification: Fleiss's kappa for annotation agreement and Pearson correlations for metric consistency are unchanged. Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals or formal significance tests for model performance.

E6.justification: Matched tables and figures retain the same results. For example, Table 4 reports overall scores of 50.03 for OmniSearch (GPT-4V), 41.20 for OmniSearch (Qwen-VL-Chat), and 55.12 for humans in both versions. v3 Tables 11–16 become v4 Tables 10–15 without result changes.

T1.justification: The dataset/category definitions and mathematical descriptions are unchanged. No formal assumptions, theorems, proofs or derivations are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements and conclusion retain the same claims about dynamic VQA, heuristic retrieval limitations and OmniSearch's novelty and effectiveness. Shortening the first contribution bullet does not change its scientific scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning adaptive planning, over-retrieval, language/search bias and scalability are retained. Appendix E.3 preserves the limitations involving long contexts, incomplete retrieval chains and insufficiently precise visual retrieval.

D1.justification: v4 removes v3 Appendix C.4 and Table 10, eliminating the exact Chinese/English prompts for original models, heuristic mRAGs and OmniSearch, including central instructions for the prompting-based GPT-4V implementation. Footnote 1 instead reports released code and data with a repository link. Training and hardware details remain, but C.3 still points to the deleted prompt subsection.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 adds comparisons with text-domain agentic RAG and Chen et al.'s multimodal causal framework, and introduces the ReWOO reference. ReAct and Chen et al. were already cited in v3's prompt discussion; the broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v4 updates authors, affiliations and publication headers, adds acknowledgements, lightly rewrites a contribution bullet and footnote, and removes the prompt subsection. The overall narrative remains intact, although C.3 and Section 6.2 retain stale cross-references.

P2.justification: The prompt table is removed, Figure 3's retained running example is recolored and rasterized, and Figure 1 and several appendix displays are repositioned. All eight figures remain; subsequent result tables are renumbered with their contents preserved.

improvement.justification: The release link and clearer agentic-RAG positioning provide benefits, while removing the exact bilingual prompts weakens reproducibility within the PDF and leaves a dangling reference in C.3. The scientific evidence is unchanged. The supplied PDFs do not establish whether the linked release compensates for the omitted implementation instructions, so the net quality effect remains uncertain.
